title: CPF (Amendment) Bill — transfer of Singtel Special Discounted Shares to CDP accounts
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading that amends the CPF Act to enable the transfer of Singtel Special Discounted Shares from the CPF Board to CDP accounts of SDS holders.
why_it_matters: The Bill enables the transfer of Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to CDP accounts for around 615,000 SDS holders, planned for November 2026. Holders with individual CDP accounts will have their shares transferred there, while those without will have designated CDP accounts created under their names. Holders may sell and receive proceeds in their CPF Ordinary Account or in cash, with CPF withdrawal conditions waived from 8 April 2026.

key_points.point: The Bill is moved for Second Reading.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: That the Bill be now read a Second time

key_points.point: MOM assessed no conflict of interest for Members holding Singtel shares to debate and vote on the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: there is no conflict of interest for Members holding Singtel shares to participate in this debate and to vote on the Bill

key_points.point: The Minister declares he holds Singtel SDS as a CPF member.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: I declare that I am a holder of Singtel Special Discounted Shares (Singtel SDS) as a Central Provident Fund (CPF) member.

key_points.point: The Bill updates a legacy arrangement to transfer Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to CDP accounts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: It updates a legacy arrangement by enabling the transfer of Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to the Central Depository (CDP) accounts of SDS holders.

key_points.point: The SDS scheme was introduced in 1993.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The SDS scheme was introduced in 1993 to give Singaporeans a stake in Singapore's economic success through share ownership.

key_points.point: Before the exercise, there were around 615,000 SDS holders, whose holdings were less than 5% of Singtel's total shareholdings.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: there were around 615,000 SDS holders, whose SDS holdings collectively represented less than 5% of Singtel's total shareholdings.

key_points.point: The median SDS holder had around 1,360 shares worth about $6,800 in equity value.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The median SDS holder had around 1,360 shares that were worth about $6,800 in equity value.

key_points.point: The transfer is planned for November 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The transfer is planned for November 2026.

key_points.point: Holders with individual CDP accounts will have their Singtel SDS automatically transferred there.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: we will automatically transfer their Singtel SDS to their individual CDP accounts.

key_points.point: Holders without CDP accounts will have their Singtel SDS automatically transferred to designated CDP accounts under their names.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: we will automatically transfer their Singtel SDS to designated CDP accounts under their respective names

key_points.point: The designated account will only hold Singtel SDS and related entitlements.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: This account will be created specifically to only hold Singtel SDS and its related entitlements.

key_points.point: SDS holders will continue to receive future dividends in their CPF Ordinary Accounts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: They will continue to receive future dividends in their CPF Ordinary Accounts.

key_points.point: If they sell, holders can opt to receive sale proceeds in their CPF Ordinary Accounts or in cash.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: they can opt to receive the sale proceeds either in their CPF Ordinary Accounts or in cash.

key_points.point: The CPF Board decided to allow those who sell their SDS to withdraw proceeds in cash without having met CPF withdrawal conditions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: the CPF Board has reviewed its rules and decided to allow those who sell their SDS to withdraw their proceeds in cash if they wish to do so without having met CPF withdrawal conditions.

key_points.point: This was effected from 8 April 2026 through subsidiary legislation amendments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: We have effected this from 8 April 2026 through subsidiary legislation amendments.

key_points.point: All SDS holders would have received a hard copy notification letter in April 2026 from the CPF Board and Singtel Group.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: All SDS holders would have received a hard copy notification letter in April 2026, issued jointly by the CPF Board and Singtel Group.

key_points.point: Touchpoints include a dedicated hotline, website, SingPost branches and CPF service centres.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: These span multiple channels, including a dedicated hotline, website, SingPost branches and CPF service centres across Singapore.

key_points.point: Over 20,000 SDS holders were identified for targeted outreach.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: we have identified over 20,000 SDS holders who may require greater assistance.

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: I rise to support the Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay declares his interest as an SDS holder.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: I declare my interest as an SDS holder.

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay cites median SDS figures: about $2,000 paid, about $6,800 worth as at April, and about $5,000 in cumulative dividends.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: The median SDS holder paid about $2,000 for the shares; they are worth about $6,800 as at April and have received about $5,000 in cumulative dividends.

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay asks whether odd lots will make it harder to sell without topping up.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: Will this make it harder for them to sell without topping up?

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay asks whether sale charges will be higher than under CPF Board.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: Will these sale charges be higher than what they enjoy today when held via CPF Board?

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay asks what measures protect holders from scammers exploiting the transfer exercise.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: What measures are in place to protect them from scammers who may exploit this entire transfer exercise?

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: I support the Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi asks why designated CDP accounts are used instead of standard individual CDP accounts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: why the Government has chosen to create designated CDP accounts for the sole purpose of holding Singtel SDS for these SDS holders, instead of simply seeking the consent of SDS holders to create standard individual CDP accounts and transfer the SDS into these accounts for them?

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi cites commission rates of 0.24% through Philips Securities or a flat fee of $17.95 through SingPost.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: Currently, the commission rates are 0.24%, if the shares are sold through Philips Securities, or a flat fee of $17.95 cents if sold through SingPost.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi cites low-cost brokers offering rates as low as 0.03% or flat fees of around $1 to $2.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: Meanwhile, low-cost brokers in the market offer rates as low as 0.03%, or even flat fees of around $1 to $2.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi asks whether fees will be waived for very elderly SDS holders selling small amounts through SingPost.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: Will the Government consider waiving the fees for the very elderly SDS holders that are selling only small amounts of shares through SingPost

key_points.point: Mr Louis Chua says the Workers' Party supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: The Workers' Party supports this Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Louis Chua declares he holds regular Singtel shares.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: I do have regular Singtel shares.

key_points.point: Mr Louis Chua cites a $2,000 investment growing to nearly $12,000 in total value today.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: a $2,000 investment in Singtel SDS has grown into nearly $12,000 in total value today, comprising $5,000 in cumulative dividends and $6,800 worth of shares as at 1 April 2026.

key_points.point: Mr Louis Chua says SDS outperformed the CPF Ordinary Account by a factor of 2.6 times.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: the SDS has outperformed the CPF Ordinary Account by a factor of 2.6 times.

key_points.point: Mr Louis Chua asks for the rationale for treating SDS proceeds differently.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: what is the Government's rationale for why the SDS proceeds are treated differently?

key_points.point: Ms Gho Sze Kee supports the Bill with reservations.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
key_points.quote: But notwithstanding, I support the Bill.

key_points.point: Ms Gho Sze Kee says allowing a direct cash-out departs from a long-standing CPF principle.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
key_points.quote: By allowing a direct cash-out today, we are departing from this long-standing principle.

key_points.point: Ms Gho Sze Kee notes media reports of about 20,000 members with low CPF balances and no CDP accounts.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
key_points.quote: The media reported about 20,000 members with low CPF balances and no CDP accounts.

key_points.point: Ms Gho Sze Kee explains MRSS matches voluntary top-ups of up to $2,000 a year dollar-for-dollar.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
key_points.quote: Under MRSS, every dollar voluntarily topped up to $2,000 a year, will be matched dollar-for-dollar by the Government.

key_points.point: Ms Gho Sze Kee suggests automatic MRSS matching for eligible shareholders who sweep part of their proceeds into CPF retirement savings.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
key_points.quote: Can the Government consider automatic MRSS matching for eligible shareholders who voluntarily choose to sweep part of their proceeds into their CPF retirement savings.

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim says the Bill will have his support.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: the Bill will have my support.

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asks whether the process for deceased shareholders will be more inaccessible after transfer to individual CDP accounts.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: Would the process be even more inaccessible now after the transfer to individual CDP accounts?

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asks whether CPF nominations continue to apply after shares are transferred to CDP.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: Will the CPF nomination originally made by members continue to apply after the shares are transferred to CDP?

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asks how the Government will pursue its duty of care on financial illiteracy.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: how the Government will pursue its duty of care to ensure that this unlocking of wealth does not go awry owing to financial illiteracy.

key_points.point: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim notes there have been no further efforts to offer discounted shares to the public since the first step.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: But since that first step, there have been no further efforts to offer discounted shares to the public.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: Sir, with that, I support the Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong says the Bill is a significant shift in responsibility from the system to the individual.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: It is a significant shift in responsibility: from the system to the individual.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong flags the risk of premature liquidation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: First, the risk of premature liquidation.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong flags the heightened risk of scams and mis-selling.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: Third, and of particular concern, is the heightened risk of scams and mis-selling.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong suggests a clear prompt or short cooling-off period at first sale.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: there could be a clear prompt or a short cooling-off period.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong recommends a post-implementation review.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: Finally, I would recommend a post-implementation review.

key_points.point: Mr Saktiandi Supaat supports the Bill but has clarifications and suggestions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: I support the Bill, but I have a few clarifications and suggestions.

key_points.point: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asks why there have not been many more initiatives since the SDS scheme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: why have we not seen much more initiatives since then?

key_points.point: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asks what triggered the need for the transfer at this point in time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: what triggered the need for this transfer at this point in time?

key_points.point: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asks why the general rule requiring the Full Retirement Sum at age 55 is not applied.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: What is the reason for not applying the general rule that assets in the CPF system can only be withdrawn after the member has set aside the Full Retirement Sum at age 55?

key_points.point: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asks how many SDS holders have sold and how many withdrew cash versus retaining proceeds in CPF.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: Could the Minister share how many SDS holders have sold their shares since the announcement and how many have withdrawn proceeds in cash versus retaining them within CPF?

key_points.point: Mr Shawn Loh supports the Central Provident Fund (Amendment) Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
key_points.quote: I support the Central Provident Fund (Amendment) Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Shawn Loh asks the Ministry to share an evaluation of the programme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
key_points.quote: I hope that the Ministry can share an evaluation of the programme, both where it went well and areas for improvement.

key_points.point: Mr Shawn Loh asks how long physical touchpoints will operate.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
key_points.quote: Can the Government clarify how long any physical touchpoints will be operating for?

key_points.point: Mr Shawn Loh asks whether Silver Generation ambassadors will be empowered to direct seniors to financial advice channels.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
key_points.quote: Can the Government confirm that Silver Generation ambassadors will also be empowered to direct our seniors to channels to receive appropriate financial advice?

key_points.point: Mr Shawn Loh suggests considering closing the CPF Investment Scheme for the Special Account.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
key_points.quote: it is time to consider closing the CPF Investment Scheme for the Special Account

key_points.point: The Minister says there are no plans to extend the SDS scheme as of now.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: there are no plans to extend this scheme as of now.

key_points.point: The Minister says the scheme had achieved its intended objectives.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: By these measures, the scheme had achieved its intended objectives.

key_points.point: The Minister says three in five SDS holders have CDP accounts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: Today, three in five SDS holders have CDP accounts.

key_points.point: The Minister says the transfer will give SDS holders greater flexibility to consolidate shareholdings in CDP accounts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The upcoming transfer will benefit SDS holders by giving them greater flexibility to consolidate their shareholdings in their CDP accounts.

key_points.point: The Minister says Singtel will be able to communicate directly with shareholders and execute corporate actions more timely and cost-efficiently.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: After the transfer, Singtel will be able to communicate with shareholders directly and execute corporate actions, such as scrip dividends, in a more timely and cost-efficient manner.

key_points.point: The Minister says SDS sale proceeds will not be subject to CPF withdrawal rules because the scheme met its intent of enhancing CPF members' assets.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: We decided that the SDS sale proceeds would not be subject to the CPF withdrawal rules given that the SDS scheme has met its intent of enhancing the assets of CPF members.

key_points.point: As of end April, around 81,000 SDS holders, or 13%, had sold their shares.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: As of end April, around 81,000 SDS holders, or 13%, have sold their shares.

key_points.point: Around nine in 10 chose to receive proceeds in cash.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: Around nine in 10 chose to receive the proceeds in cash.

key_points.point: The Minister says odd lots can be sold through channels such as Phillip Securities at the same rates as today.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: Singtel SDS, including odd lots, can be sold through channels such as Phillip Securities at the same rates as today.

key_points.point: The Minister says SDS holders are not limited to selling via SingPost or Phillip Securities; it is up to SGX brokers whether to facilitate sales.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: SDS holders are not limited to selling via SingPost or Phillip Securities as it is up to the Singapore Exchange brokers whether or not they wish to facilitate the sale of Singtel SDS, which also includes costs.

key_points.point: The Minister says about 95% of sales transactions are done online by seniors.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: about 95% of sales transactions are actually done online by them

key_points.point: The Minister says the Government cannot open individual CDP accounts on SDS holders' behalf.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: The Government also cannot open individual CDP accounts on SDS holders' behalf.

key_points.point: The Minister says opening individual CDP accounts requires compliance screenings including tax residency declarations and risk appetite assessments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: Doing so requires the members to complete comprehensive compliance screenings, including tax residency declarations and risk appetite assessments to ensure adherence to regulatory requirements and international tax obligations are fulfilled.

key_points.point: The Minister says SDS holders may go to more than 30 SingPost branches or any of five CPF Service Centres for assistance.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: SDS holders may go to more than 30 SingPost branches for assistance with the sale of their shares, or any of the five CPF Service Centres for general assistance.

key_points.point: A dedicated hotline, 1713, has been set up.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: A dedicated hotline, 1713, has been set up for those who prefer to seek help over the phone.

key_points.point: CPF Board and Singtel are partnering AIC for door-to-door outreach and visits to nursing homes and care facilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: CPF Board and Singtel are partnering the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) to conduct door-to-door outreach and visits to nursing homes and care facilities.

key_points.point: For designated CDP accounts, upon a holder's passing, Singtel SDS will be handled in accordance with CPF nomination rules.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: following the transfer for SDS holders who have designated CDP accounts upon their passing, their Singtel SDS will be handled in accordance with CPF nomination rules.

key_points.point: For individual CDP accounts, Singtel SDS will be treated as any other CDP shares and form part of the estate.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: For those who have individual CDP accounts, their Singtel SDS will be treated as any other CDP shares and will form part of their estate.

key_points.point: Sale proceeds will be credited only to the holder's bank account registered with CPF Board or via PayNow-NRIC registered bank account.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: sale proceeds will be credited only to SDS holders' bank account registered with the CPF Board or via their PayNow-NRIC registered bank account.

key_points.point: CPF Board and Singtel will never ask for bank account details or payment in connection with the exercise.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: CPF Board and Singtel will never ask or never request bank account details or any payment from SDS holders in connection with this exercise.

key_points.point: The Minister says no complaints about residents being scammed have been received thus far.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: we have, thankfully, not received any complaints about residents being scammed thus far.

key_points.point: The Minister says the new investment scheme is being developed further and details will be shared in due course.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: We are developing the scheme further and will share details and updates in due course.

key_points.point: The Minister says almost 70% of SDS holders were from HDB background and 30% from the private sector.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: almost 70% of people who have the SDS Singtel accounts were from HDB background and dwelling, including myself, and 30% belong to the private sector.

key_points.point: The Minister concludes the Bill recognises it is timely to update the legacy arrangement by transferring SDS Singtel shares from CPF Board to CDP accounts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: this Bill recognises that it is timely to update this legacy arrangement by enabling the transfer of SDS Singtel shares from the CPF Board to their CDP accounts.

what_happens_next: The transfer of Singtel SDS to CDP accounts is planned for November 2026; the transcript does not state the next parliamentary step after the Second Reading debate.
not_said: Whether the Bill will be read a Third time and when it will come into force.
How many SDS holders have not engaged with outreach efforts so far.
Whether sale charges will be higher than under CPF Board for future sales.
Whether fees will be waived for very elderly SDS holders selling small amounts through SingPost.
What the policy logic is for treating SDS proceeds differently from housing and CPFIS investments on accrued interest.
Whether the Government will consider automatic MRSS matching for eligible shareholders.
Whether there will be a formal post-implementation review of the transfer.
How long physical touchpoints will operate and whether Silver Generation ambassadors will be empowered.
What the administrative costs of the SDS scheme were and what resource savings will follow closure.
Whether there will be further broad-based share ownership or discounted share schemes tied to other GLC listings.
What details of the upcoming new investment scheme will be and when they will be shared.
Whether the CPF Investment Scheme for the Special Account will be closed or the Special Account renamed.
